claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic Cu–Ni–Pd–Pt multi-principal-element alloy.
The near-equiatomic Cu–Ni–Pd–Pt catalyst has low platinum-group-metal content.
A porous CeO2 overlayer will be deposited on the alloy by atomic layer deposition.
The CeO2 overlayer will be 2–5 nm thick and deposited at approximately 150 °C.
The ALD treatment will produce a conformal, porous CeO2 layer.
The CeO2 layer will act as an oxygen buffer.
The CeO2 layer will act as a physical barrier protecting the underlying alloy.
Enhanced oxygen-storage capacity from the CeO2 overlayer will promote oxidation reactions at low temperatures.
The CeO2 overlayer will physically stabilize the alloy and reduce sintering.
Reduced sintering will limit the loss of active sites during aging.
Selective adsorption or exclusion by the CeO2 overlayer will mitigate H2O poisoning.
Selective adsorption or exclusion by the CeO2 overlayer will mitigate NO poisoning.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will have a lower light-off temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will retain more activity in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will have greater long-term durability under transient and aging conditions than the unmodified catalyst.
Adding the CeO2 overlayer will not increase platinum-group-metal use.
The predicted improvements apply during transient operation below 150 °C with exposure to H2O and NO and during periodic aging.
An excessively dense CeO2 layer could block active sites and limit the improvement.

contradictions.description: A near-equiatomic four-element Cu–Ni–Pd–Pt alloy would contain approximately 50 at.% total Pd plus Pt, which conflicts with describing its alloy composition as having low PGM content unless 'low' instead refers to total catalyst loading; no such distinction is provided.
